Q: How to calculate square root in cmd? A:

This code will be quicker because it does a binary search, instead of the iteration method above.
Be warned CMD uses 32 bit signed integers so the answer is not exact for many cases.

@echo off

Set Number=%1
Set MinRoot=1
REM square root of max signed int32 rounded up
Set /a MaxRoot=46341
Set /a Delta=MaxRoot-MinRoot

:Loop
  Set /a TryRoot=(MaxRoot - MinRoot) / 2 + MinRoot
  REM Echo TryRoot=%TryRoot%, Delta=%Delta%
  Set /a Test=TryRoot * TryRoot
  If %Test% EQU %Number% goto Found
  If %Test% GTR %Number% Set MaxRoot=%TryRoot%
  If %Test% LSS %Number% Set MinRoot=%TryRoot%
  Set /a Delta=MaxRoot-MinRoot
If Not "%Delta%"=="1" If Not %MaxRoot%==%MinRoot% goto Loop
REM Echo Past loop

:Found
Set Root=%MaxRoot%
Set /a Error=Number-(Root * Root)
REM Echo Max=%MaxRoot% Min=%MinRoot%
Echo Found Number=%Number%, Root=%Root%, Error=%Error%

Q: Best way to reject multipart Content-Type on text-only POST endpoints in a PHP MVC middleware pipeline? A:

This is a custom PHP MVC framework (not a well-known one like Laravel, Symfony, or CodeIgniter). The core framework lives under system/ (custom Dispatcher, Controller base class, Model base, Middleware pipeline) with some third-party libraries:

  • League Plates for templating
  • Symfony HttpFoundation for Request/Response objects
  • Symfony Mailer for email

The middleware pipeline and routing are all custom-built. There is no framework-provided "add Content-Type validation middleware" method or kernel event subscriber to hook into. This is why I'm evaluating the three approaches (new middleware class, extend base controller, or modify the Dispatcher) rather than looking for a framework-native solution.

Q: process.env.PORT is undefined (in LinuxCloud environment) A:

If you don't want to use external dotenv packages to load the env file , you could use the loadEnvFile function from the node:process . process.env is just access to system variables set in the environment , some of these are default like NODE_ENV and sometimes you have to manually set it up . For env files , they're just normal files which node doesn't know but bring them in , you have to load them with dotenv or loadEnvFile

const {loadEnvFile} = require('node:process')
loadEnvFile()
console.log(process.env.PORT)

Q: DynamoDb get item the number of conditions on the keys is invalid A:

You must provide the name of the partition key attribute and a single value for that attribute. Query returns all items with that partition key value. Optionally, you can provide a sort key attribute and use a comparison operator to refine the search results.more

get(params, callback) ⇒ AWS.Request
Returns a set of attributes for the item with the given primary key by delegating to AWS.DynamoDB.getItem().

In SessionsTable id is HASH key and in SessionsDynamoDbTable id in RANGE key.for SessionsDynamoDbTable you should provide HASH Key in addition to RANGE key.
